# Fixture Classifier, first edition

This document is a test fixture. It is not a publication and contains no clinical
information. Every gene symbol in it is invented, so that nothing here can be
mistaken for evidence about a real gene if it escapes the test suite.

## Section 1 — Entity definition

GENEA mutation defines Fixture Entity One when the blast count is at least 20 per
cent; a blast count of 10 to 19 per cent is assigned to Fixture Entity Two. The
criterion is defeated where a fixture-defining fusion is present.

GENEB mutation refines an existing category but does not move it.

## Section 2 — Prognostic table

| Gene | Effect | Adjustment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GENEA | favourable in the fixture cohort | multivariable-adjusted for age and blast count |
| GENEC | no independent effect after adjustment | multivariable-adjusted |

GENEC was reported as adverse in an earlier fixture series on univariable
analysis only.

## Section 3 — Follow-up marker

The GENEA mutation is a validated fixture follow-up marker and should be tracked
with a high-sensitivity assay. GENEB is not validated as a stand-alone follow-up
marker in this fixture setting.

## Section 4 — Predisposition

A near-heterozygous loss-of-function GENED variant with a lower-burden second
event is the characteristic fixture predisposition architecture, and warrants
confirmation on a non-haematopoietic specimen.
